evals.prompt: Our checkout endpoint started returning total: null for some carts since yesterday's release. I pasted a failing request body in fixtures/cart-4471.json. Can you fix it? The code is in src/checkout/.
evals.expected_output: The agent builds a repro command from the fixture before editing code, traces the null back to where it is produced, fixes it there, and adds a regression test.
expectations: Runs a concrete repro command (test, curl, or script using fixtures/cart-4471.json) and shows it failing before any source edit
Checks recent changes (git log/diff for the release) as evidence
States a root cause naming a file and line or function
The fix is at the origin of the null, not a null-coalescing default at the response layer
Adds or proposes a regression test that fails without the fix

evals.prompt: This is urgent, the demo is in 20 minutes. `npm test` fails in tests/pricing.test.ts with 'expected 90 received 89.99999'. Just make it pass, I don't care how.
evals.expected_output: Under time pressure the agent still reproduces the single failing test, identifies the floating-point root cause, and fixes the computation (for example integer cents or explicit rounding at the right boundary) instead of loosening the assertion.
expectations: Runs only the single failing test file to reproduce
Names floating-point arithmetic in a specific computation as the root cause
Does not change the test's expected value or weaken the assertion to make it pass
Reports root cause, fix, and evidence of the test passing

evals.prompt: I've already tried three fixes for the websocket reconnect bug (added a retry, increased the timeout, and wrapped the handler in try/catch). It still drops messages after reconnect. Try something else?
evals.expected_output: The agent recognises the three-strikes condition, stops proposing a fourth patch, returns to evidence gathering and questions the reconnect design, and reports what has been ruled out.
expectations: Explicitly declines to propose a fourth symptom patch before gathering new evidence
Identifies that the retry, timeout, and try/catch attempts treated symptoms
Proposes building a repro loop for message loss across a reconnect
Raises an architectural question (e.g. message buffering or acknowledgement across reconnect)
